title: website — Base Website/CMS Module
key_finding: Community edition fully supports multiple websites per database behind a feature-group toggle; each website has isolated routing maps, domain-based resolution, and website-scoped publication states.

models_researched.description: Core website record: domain, company, languages, CDN, social, menu, public user

multi_website.activation: Automatic when second website record is created

migration_risks.detail: website.domain has a unique constraint. Cloning or importing website records requires explicit domain deconfliction.
website.company_id is required. Multi-company migrations must pre-assign company records before website records can be created or restored.
Creating a second website record automatically implies website.group_multi_website for all website designer users. This may surface UI elements the customer has not configured for.
Records with is_published=True may appear unpublished when accessed in a different website context. Post-migration validation must verify publication per website scope, not just at DB level.
_get_current_website_id is ormcache'd by domain_name+fallback. After migration, caches must be invalidated to pick up new domain-to-website mappings.

website.visitor and website.track can be large tables. Cron _cron_unlink_old_visitors hard-deletes (not archives) old records. Migration should plan for table size and decide whether historical visitor data is needed.
mega_menu_content is stored as raw HTML without sanitisation. Content migration must preserve HTML verbatim; any re-rendering or sanitisation will corrupt the menus.
website.rewrite records have an optional website_id. Rules without a website_id apply to all websites. Migration must audit which rules need website assignment.
